name: Sasak
notes: Sasak (Bahasa Sasak), spoken by ~2.7 million on Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia (Austronesian, Malayo-Polynesian; closely related to Balinese and Sumbawa). Five dialects with low mutual intelligibility (Kutó-Kuté, Nggetó-Nggeté, Menó-Mené, Ngenó-Ngené, Meriaq-Meriku); this spec is a dialect-neutral basic-quality description, not tied to one variety. Traditionally written in the Sasak script (aksara Sasaq, an abugida), now largely superseded by a Latin orthography adapted from Indonesian conventions. CONSONANTS: /p b t d k ɡ/ plosives, /tɕ dʑ/ (⟨c⟩/⟨j⟩) alveo-palatal affricates, /m n ɲ ŋ/ nasals (⟨ny⟩/⟨ng⟩ digraphs), /s h/ fricatives, /r/ rhotic (realised [r]~[ɾ]), /l w j/ approximants (⟨y⟩ for /j/, ⟨j⟩ reserved for the affricate). VOWELS: eight vowel qualities across dialects; the Latin orthography marks the front-vowel contrast diacritically — unmarked ⟨e⟩ = schwa /ə/, ⟨é⟩ = /e/, ⟨è⟩ = /ɛ/ — a convention shared with other Nusantara Malayo-Polynesian orthographies (cf. Indonesian ⟨e⟩). Six diphthongs /ae ai au ia uə oe/ are attested; the back-vowel diacritic pair ⟨ó⟩/⟨ò⟩ used in some dictionaries for a parallel /o/–/ɔ/ contrast is not modelled here for lack of a consistently sourced mapping. Glottal stop /ʔ/ is present in the phoneme inventory but its orthographic representation (apostrophe vs. unmarked) is not confidently sourced and is left unmodelled; word-final /k/ neutralisation is plausible by areal analogy with neighbouring Malayo-Polynesian languages but is not asserted without a citation.
